name: Solar Orbiter
first: First mission designed to image the Sun's polar regions in detail; complements Parker Solar Probe's in-corona measurements with high-latitude remote sensing
description: ESA-led mission with a NASA launch and one instrument contribution. Where Parker Solar Probe goes closer than anyone has ever been, Solar Orbiter goes higher — using repeated Venus gravity assists over a decade to climb out of the ecliptic toward ~33° heliographic inclination. From that vantage point its instrument suite (PHI, EUI, SPICE, STIX, METIS, SoloHI + four in-situ packages) images the Sun's polar magnetic fields, traces solar-wind acceleration in real time, and links remote and in-situ measurements simultaneously. First perihelion 2020-06-15 at 0.51 AU. Closest perihelion to date 2022-10-12 at 0.29 AU (inside Mercury's perihelion).
